> EmptyDir::TearDownAt was called indeeded, but the not-yet-exiting process of init containers created the empty-dir again and put some files under this dir.

Could it be that TearDown is called earlier than needed, i.e. when container process still uses the directory? If this is the case, it should probably be called when all processes are finished.

In any case this should be covered by e2e tests. Please, add.

issue_context.title: empty-dir directories was not cleaned after pod deleted
issue_context.body:
### What happened? When a pod with empty-dir volumes is deleted just after it was created, it's possible that the init containers still write contents to empty-dirs. And this might cause empty-dirs orphaned and kubelet could no delete it by rmdir. ### What did you expect to happen? empty-dirs should be deleted forcely. ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? It's not easy to reproduce this issue. A possible way is that: 1. Create pod with empty-dir volumes and an init container which mounts and writes many contents to this volume 2. Delete the pod after init container just started. ### Anything else we need to know? _No response_ ### Kubernetes version 1.20 ### Cloud provider
### OS version
```console # On Linux: $ cat /etc/os-release # paste output here $ uname -a # paste output here # On Windows: C:\> wmic os get Caption, Version, BuildNumber, OSArchitecture # paste output here ```
### Install tools
### Container runtime (CRI) and version (if applicable)
### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)

review_comments: Function description should be updated. It states that "it effectively does a recursive rmdir instead of RemoveAll", which is not the case anymore.

Please bear in mind that using `RemoveAll` instead of `Rmdir` might slow down the execution which is part of the kubelet's main sync loop iteration. I'm not saying it's wrong, just that IIUC this code was written with an assumption that no files exist anymore. We should be careful here.
